title: CSE-307 Operating Systems Master Question Bank
description: Comprehensive question bank covering Virtual Memory, Address Translation, TLB, Page Faults, and Disk Scheduling.

questions.title: Virtual Memory Paging Purpose
questions.prompt: What is the primary advantage of virtual memory paging compared to simple contiguous memory allocation?
questions.explanation: Paging divides physical memory into fixed-size frames and logical memory into pages, completely eliminating external fragmentation and allowing non-contiguous allocation.

options.text: It completely eliminates internal fragmentation in all memory allocations
It allows a process's physical address space to be non-contiguous, eliminating external fragmentation
It avoids having to load any page tables into physical memory
It makes disk access faster than RAM access

questions.title: Paging vs Segmentation Characteristics
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements correctly describe Paging? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Paging uses fixed-sized blocks determined by hardware, invisible to the programmer, and eliminates external fragmentation while suffering from slight internal fragmentation.

options.text: Page sizes are fixed by hardware architecture (typically powers of 2)
The programmer is explicitly responsible for defining page boundaries
Paging suffers from internal fragmentation within the final allocated page
Paging produces severe external fragmentation requiring periodic compaction

questions.title: Effective Memory Access Time with TLB
questions.prompt: Assume memory access takes 100 ns and TLB access takes 20 ns. If the TLB hit ratio is 80% (0.80) and a page fault does not occur, what is the Effective Access Time (EAT) in nanoseconds?
questions.explanation: EAT = Hit_Ratio * (TLB_time + Mem_time) + Miss_Ratio * (TLB_time + 2 * Mem_time) = 0.8 * (20 + 100) + 0.2 * (20 + 200) = 0.8 * 120 + 0.2 * 220 = 96 + 44 = 140 ns.

questions.title: Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) Function
questions.prompt: What is the primary role of the Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) in modern computer systems?
questions.explanation: The TLB is a fast, hardware associative cache that stores recent virtual-to-physical page translations, avoiding an extra memory access to the page table.

options.text: A hardware cache storing recently accessed page-table entries to speed up address translation
A disk buffer storing swap space pages awaiting dirty writeback
A software table managed by the scheduler to track thread states
An execution pipeline cache storing decoded machine instructions

questions.title: Page Fault Exception Handling
questions.prompt: What sequence of events is initiated by the CPU when a requested page's Valid/Invalid bit is set to 'Invalid'?
questions.explanation: An invalid page reference triggers a hardware trap/interrupt to the operating system kernel (page fault), which suspends the process, issues disk I/O to fetch the page, updates the page table, and restarts the faulting instruction.

options.text: Hardware page fault trap to OS -> Process saved -> Disk I/O fetches page -> Frame allocated -> Page table updated -> Restart instruction
The CPU immediately halts execution and shuts down physical memory
The MMU ignores the address and returns byte 0x00 to the accumulator
The process is immediately terminated without checking backing store

questions.title: Paging Address Translation Visual Simulation
questions.prompt: Use the interactive MMU and Page Table visualization to translate the requested logical address into its physical RAM address.
questions.explanation: Address 3 decimal = 11 binary. Page = 1, Offset = 1. Page Table entry for Page 1 points to Frame 4 (100 binary). Combining Frame 4 and Offset 1 yields 1001 binary = 9 decimal.

questions.title: Belady's Anomaly in FIFO Page Replacement
questions.prompt: Belady's Anomaly states that under FIFO page replacement, increasing the number of allocated page frames can sometimes lead to an increase in the number of page faults.
questions.explanation: True. Belady's anomaly occurs in FIFO because FIFO is not a stack-based algorithm like LRU or Optimal.

questions.title: Handling a Page Fault Sequence
questions.prompt: Order the following steps taken by the OS and hardware when handling a page fault, from first (top) to last (bottom):
questions.explanation: Correct order: 1. CPU encounters invalid bit & traps to OS; 2. OS saves process registers; 3. OS locates page on disk; 4. OS reads page into free physical frame; 5. OS updates page table to valid; 6. CPU restarts instruction.

items.text: CPU attempts memory access and triggers hardware trap to OS
OS saves CPU registers and process state
OS checks internal table to verify valid reference and locates page on backing store
OS issues I/O read to transfer page into an available physical frame
OS modifies page table entry to valid and sets frame number

questions.title: Contiguous Memory Allocation Strategies
questions.prompt: Match each contiguous memory allocation algorithm with its definition:
questions.explanation: First-Fit allocates the first hole that is big enough; Best-Fit allocates the smallest hole that is big enough; Worst-Fit allocates the largest available hole.

pairs.right: Allocates the first hole in memory that is large enough
Allocates the smallest hole that is large enough, minimizing leftover hole size
Allocates the largest hole available, leaving the largest remaining fragment
